label: Dispatch I
gaelic_opener: "Cum do bhreacan tioram, a charaid—tha na coilltean a' bruidhinn a-nochd."
title: Mud on the Pine-Edge & Three Hours of Turnip Broth
excerpt: Found salt-crinkled inside a brass-capped leather scroll tube after a wet crossing off the northern ridge.
paragraphs: ("Keep your plaid dry, friend—the woods are speaking tonight.")

The snowmelt up on Druim nan Càrn came down harder than expected this morning. By midday the little burn east of the pines had swollen knee-deep, spinning Na Brùnaich's soup-stirrer waterwheels so fast I thought old Tam's roof turf was going to take flight.

I meant only to trade two bundles of dry peat for whetstone oil and be back on the trail before dusk. Three hours later I was still wedged beneath a mossy lintel holding a third wooden bowl of turnip broth while two brothers argued over whose great-grandfather carved the cleaner Còinneach-Thorc tile for Sia-Clachan.

On the walk back through the wet ferns I crossed fresh spade-tusk furrows near the creek bend—still filling slowly with rain—and heard Giùthas-Ghob scolding from the upper canopy before I ever saw what spooked them. Whatever moved along the water bank left no sound in the moss.
I am tying your copper hearth bead onto the strap now and sending the falcon aloft before the squall rolls in from the loch. Keep a scrap of fish on the roost-box for her.
signoff: — Inked by peatlight, an unnamed Way-Warden
